statements.title: the central root of unity η_μ already lies in the ring of the column
the ring of a column is Z[ζ_m] ⊗ C_T, and its index is a power of p
locally at p, C_T is the monomial ring of the numerical semigroup S_T, and δ(T) is its number of gaps
when p > (n−1)(n−2), or n ≤ 12, the semigroup is read in F_p from the nonzero power sums M_{hj}(T)
the index of a column is p^{φ(m) · #gaps of S_T}
a column ring is Gorenstein if and only if its semigroup is symmetric
if the conductor is at most e, then p·O_μ ⊆ A_μ; always so when p > (n−1)(n−2)
the vacuum column is maximal: A_0 = O_0 at every prime height
level–rank duality replaces T by −(F_p ∖ T) and keeps the semigroup
the conformal weight sees M₂ and no more; with trivial stabiliser, δ = 1 iff M₂M₃ ≠ 0
statements.formal_part: added to the Lean repository after publication (21-oct-2026, written for Part II, Corollary 3): the semigroup half of the second sentence, from the generating rule with the moments abstracted to a predicate (e ≥ 4, M₁ = 0): δ ≥ 2 ↔ M₂M₃ = 0; not the congruence M₂ ≡ |μ+ρ|², nor Theorem 3 itself

statements.title: a closed count of the maximal columns, over the multiplicative stabilisers
δ(T) ≤ (n−1)(n−2)/2, with equality exactly for the trinomials X^n + aX + b, ab ≠ 0
